result:
Your partner reverted a ruling that contradicts the spec. Under the protocol, that revert becomes a deferred item rather than a change made during plan completion. So the branch keeps the 3-slot threshold for now, and the deferred entry records the return to § 2. The other three rulings stand. The night-email question needs no change, so I record it in history only.

**1. Record the reverted ruling as a deferred item**

<edit path="specs/deferred_items.md">
## Dock alerts: restore the § 2 alert threshold (from plan 12-dock-alerts, Task 2)

- What: the alert threshold ships at 3 or fewer free slots (Task 2 ruling, commits 8c9d0e1..a4b5c6d). The partner reverted that ruling on 2026-11-18. The threshold goes back to 2 or fewer free slots, as `specs/dock-alerts.md` § 2 says.
- Why it was changed: docks refill more slowly than the design assumed, so 2 free slots leaves riders no warning.
- Cost while open: the operations team gets about one extra alert a day.
- Done when: the threshold check and its tests use 2 or fewer free slots, and nothing contradicts § 2.
</edit>

**2. Mark up the plan**

<edit path="specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md">
## Completion

Status: complete (2026-11-18). Tasks 1–4 done and reviewed. Final whole-branch review clean.

- Task 2: built at 3 or fewer free slots. The partner reverted this ruling, so the change is deferred: see `specs/deferred_items.md`, "Dock alerts: restore the § 2 alert threshold".
- Task 3: the module is `alerts/notify.py`, not `alerts/send.py`, because `send` shadows the socket helper the service already imports. Alerts stay one email per alert, as planned. The reviewer's batching request was declined.
- Final review: the retry-jitter finding stays out, because the tests seed the jitter on purpose.
</edit>

**3. Add the history entry**

<edit path="specs/history.md">
## 2026-11-18: plan 12-dock-alerts (specs/dock-alerts.md)

- Implemented dock alerts by email, one email per alert, from `alerts/notify.py` (the plan named it `alerts/send.py`, but `send` shadows the socket helper).
- § 2 Alert threshold: the code alerts at 3 or fewer free slots, which contradicts § 2. The partner reverted this ruling, so § 2 stands unamended. Restoring 2 or fewer is a deferred item.
- § 3 Alert channel: the partner confirmed email is fine for alerts sent at night. No change.
- Rulings that stand: the batching request was declined (one email per alert). The retry-jitter finding stays out (the tests seed jitter on purpose).
</edit>

**4. Retire the plan and commit**

<command>
git mv specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md
</command>

<command>
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/history.md specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md
git commit -m "Complete plan 12-dock-alerts: mark up plan, record history, defer threshold revert"
</command>

**5. Delete the workspace**

The protocol has finished and there were no final-review fixes to merge, so the workspace can go. I would use the literal path `sdd-workspace` printed at skill start. The ledger shows it is `.sdd/12-dock-alerts`.

<command>
rm -rf .sdd/12-dock-alerts
</command>

---

**Message to partner:**

> Plan 12-dock-alerts is complete and retired to `specs/plans/completed/`.
>
> - **Task 2 threshold:** I recorded your revert as a deferred item in `specs/deferred_items.md`, as the plan-completion protocol requires. The branch still alerts at **3 or fewer** free slots until that item is done, which costs about one extra alert a day. § 2 of the spec is unchanged, and `specs/history.md` notes the gap. This is a small change; I can do it now as a follow-up task on this branch if you want.
> - **Other rulings:** `alerts/notify.py`, one email per alert, and leaving retry-jitter alone all stand. They are recorded in the plan and in history.
> - **Night alerts:** I recorded your answer that email is fine. No change was needed.
>
> The `.sdd/12-dock-alerts` workspace is deleted.
